q-ows.label: One word for a phrase
q-ows.summary: A phrase is given; pick the single word that means the same.

rules.text: Many one-word substitutions are built from a Greek or Latin root: phobia (fear), phile (lover), mis(o) (hate), anthropo (mankind). Match the root to the phrase.
rules.ok: Bibliophile: biblio (book) + phile (lover) = lover of books.
rules.bad: Bibliophobe is not the word for a lover of books; phobe means one who fears.

rules.text: Look-alike words come in sets that differ by one root: -cide (killing), -phobia (fear), omni- (all), -gamy (marriage), -cracy (rule). Fix the root first, then the prefix.
rules.ok: Patricide (father) and matricide (mother) differ only in the prefix.
rules.bad: Choosing matricide for the killing of one's father.

q-ows.cue: 'Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.'
q-ows.standard: Know the word, or break it into root parts and match them to the phrase.
q-ows.fast: Split each option into its root, discard the roots that do not match the phrase.
q-ows.eliminate: The wrong options are usually real words with a neighbouring meaning (hater instead of lover), so match both halves of the root.
traps: A word with the right root but the opposite sense (phile vs phobe).
A word that sounds similar but belongs to another phrase.

pyqs.text: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who speaks two languages fluently'.
pyqs.why: Bilingual joins bi (two) and lingua (tongue): a person who speaks two languages.

a.note: An accusation is a charge of wrongdoing; it has nothing to do with language.

b.note: A denunciation is a public condemnation of someone.

d.note: An indictment is a formal charge of a crime.

pyqs.trick: bi- means two; lingua is the tongue.

pyqs.text: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who avoids pleasures and lives with strict self-discipline'.
pyqs.why: An ascetic gives up pleasures and lives with strict self-discipline, usually for spiritual reasons.

a.note: A sceptic doubts accepted beliefs; the word says nothing about self-denial.

c.note: A mystic seeks union with God through meditation. Mystics are often ascetics too, but the phrase asks for the one who gives up pleasures, and that is the ascetic.

d.note: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known; it is about belief, not lifestyle.

pyqs.trick: Ascetic: the self-denial, not the belief, is the point.

pyqs.text: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A condition of disuse or inactivity'.
pyqs.why: Desuetude is the state of no longer being used or practised, as when a custom falls out of use.

a.note: An interregnum is the period between two reigns or governments.

b.note: Destitute means without money and basic necessities. It sounds like 'desuetude', but it describes poverty, not disuse.

c.note: Lethargy is drowsy lack of energy in a person; desuetude is about a custom or law no longer being used.

pyqs.trick: Desuetude comes from the Latin for 'to become unaccustomed': a custom no longer used.
